issues.description: The function does not validate that `todos` is an array or that it exists before calling `.filter()`. If `todos` is null, undefined, or not an array, this will throw a runtime TypeError.
issues.suggestion: Add input validation at the start of the function: if (!Array.isArray(todos)) { return []; }

issues.description: The filter callback assumes every todo item has a `text` property. If any todo object is null, undefined, or lacks a `text` property, calling `t.text.includes()` will throw a TypeError at runtime.
issues.suggestion: Add a null check in the filter predicate: return todos.filter(t => t?.text?.includes(query));

issues.description: The `query` parameter is not validated. If `query` is null or undefined, `includes(query)` will throw a TypeError. If query is not a string (e.g., a number or object), the behavior may be unexpected.
issues.suggestion: Validate and normalize the query parameter: if (!Array.isArray(todos) || typeof query !== 'string') { return []; }

issues.description: The search uses `includes()` which is case-sensitive. Users searching for 'Buy' won't find todos containing 'buy'. This is typically not the expected behavior for search functionality and leads to poor user experience.
issues.suggestion: Make the search case-insensitive: return todos.filter(t => t?.text?.toLowerCase().includes(query.toLowerCase()));

issues.description: The function creates a new array on every call using `.filter()`. For large todo lists (thousands of items), this performs O(n) filtering on each keystroke if used for real-time search, which could cause UI lag.
issues.suggestion: For real-time search, implement debouncing at the call site, or consider memoization. For very large datasets, use a search index or virtual scrolling.

issues.description: Leading/trailing whitespace in the query is not trimmed. Searching for ' buy ' won't match 'buy groceries', which is unexpected behavior for most users.
issues.suggestion: Trim the query before searching: const trimmedQuery = query.trim().toLowerCase();

issues.description: When query is an empty string or only whitespace, the function returns all todos. While technically correct, it's unclear if this is intentional behavior.
issues.suggestion: Add explicit handling for empty queries: if (trimmedQuery === '') { return todos; } with a comment explaining the behavior

codeQuality.summary: The `searchTodos` function has several critical issues that make it fragile in production use. The most significant problems are missing input validation (high severity) that will cause runtime errors when given null/undefined inputs, and lack of null-safe property access on todo items (medium severity). The case-sensitive search reduces usability. While the core logic is simple and readable, the function needs defensive programming practices including input validation, null checking, case-insensitive matching, and query trimming to be production-ready.

suggestions.description: The current code assumes every todo has a 'text' property. Using optional chaining prevents errors if the property is missing.

refactorings.summary: The search.js file contains a simple, functional search implementation that has 5 refactoring opportunities: case-insensitive search (medium impact), input validation (low impact), safe property access (medium impact), extract search strategy (high impact), and query trimming (low impact). The code works correctly but could benefit from modernization with ES6+ features (optional chaining, better string handling), defensive programming (validation), and architectural preparation for growth (extracted matching logic). The highest-impact improvement would be extracting the matching logic into a separate function, which makes the code more maintainable and extensible for future search enhancements.
